granola-vs-fathom.0: Granola vs Fathom is one of the most common head-to-head questions for US teams picking an AI note taker. Both write meeting notes for you. How they do it, though, is very different, and that difference matters more than any feature list you will find on either pricing page.
granola-vs-fathom.1: Fathom sends a recorder to your Zoom, Google Meet or Teams call and captures video, transcript and summary. Granola runs on your device instead. It listens to your computer's audio and turns your rough notes into clean ones. One is built for recording calls; the other is built for thinking during them.
granola-vs-fathom.2: Capture is the core difference. Fathom records the call (usually with a bot, with a bot-free beta), while Granola never joins the call and keeps no video. That one choice shapes price, privacy and who each tool suits.
granola-vs-fathom.3: With Granola, notes start from your own typing. You jot "pricing pushback, follow up Tuesday" and it expands that with the transcript. Fathom works the other way round, starting from the recording and then generating a summary and action items.
granola-vs-fathom.4: On price, Granola is $0 on Basic and $14 per user per month on Business. Fathom costs $0 on Free, $20 a month for Premium on monthly billing ($16 yearly), and $34 a month for Business ($25 yearly).
granola-vs-fathom.6: Take a 5-person team on annual billing. Granola Business costs $840 a year and Fathom Team costs $900 a year. The gap is small. Pick on workflow, not price.
granola-vs-fathom.7: Granola uses 0 bots. It captures audio on your device, so nobody on the call sees a recorder join. By default Fathom uses a bot, though it offers bot-free capture in beta, including on the free plan.
granola-vs-fathom.8: Client-facing work is where this matters most, since some US companies now ask vendors to keep bots out of their calls. You can still take AI-assisted notes with Granola. With Fathom you would switch to the beta bot-free mode or skip recording. Either way, tell people you are taking notes; many US states require all-party consent to record a call.
granola-vs-fathom.10: Notes can still land in your CRM with Granola Business, which connects to HubSpot, Attio and Affinity. What you do not get is video, so there is no call library for coaching. Founders doing their own sales often prefer it for exactly that reason. It feels like a notebook, not surveillance.
granola-vs-fathom.11: Privacy goes to Granola: no bot, no stored video, and a toggle to opt out of model training on every plan. Full call recordings live with Fathom, which is useful for coaching but means more sensitive data held by a vendor.
granola-vs-fathom.13: Granola Business ($14) connects to 5 named tools: Attio, Notion, HubSpot, Affinity and Zapier, plus an API and an MCP connection for AI assistants. On the other side, CRM field sync, deal views and custom summaries sit on Fathom's Business plan ($25 per user billed yearly).
granola-vs-fathom.16: Granola runs on 4 platforms: Mac and Windows for video calls, iPhone for phone calls and in-person conversations, and Android for in-person conversations since July 2026. Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams are covered by Fathom's recorder.
granola-vs-fathom.17: Because Granola listens to your device, it works with almost any meeting app that plays through your speakers. Fathom joins as a participant instead. So it behaves the same way for every person on your team, with nothing to install.
granola-vs-fathom.18: Setup takes about 5 minutes either way: sign in with Google or Microsoft, connect your calendar, and join your next meeting. The difference shows up on day 2.
granola-vs-fathom.19: Teams will find Fathom easier to standardize. Individuals who want control over what gets captured may see Granola's manual start as a feature, not a bug.
granola-vs-fathom.20: Closer to Fathom sit Fireflies ($10 per seat billed yearly) and Otter ($8.33 billed yearly), both bot-based recorders with transcripts and summaries that join from your calendar and keep a searchable record of every call.
granola-vs-fathom.22: Yes. Lynkk (our product) offers 2 capture modes: a bot that joins Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, and a Mac app plus Chrome extension that record without one. In-person conversations are covered too.
granola-vs-fathom.24: Lynkk is free for 5 notes a month (2 hours each), and Pro is $15 a month with no note cap. One honest limit: there is no Android or Windows app yet.
granola-vs-fathom.26: For a final Granola vs Fathom verdict across 3 team types: pick Fathom if you record many calls, need free unlimited recording, or coach a sales team from call clips. Private notes with no bot, written alongside the AI, point to Granola. Want both capture modes plus prep, live answers and automatic follow-up work? Pick Lynkk.
granola-vs-fathom.28: In the Granola vs Fathom debate, Granola is better for private, bot-free notes that start from what you type. For recording calls, sharing clips and syncing to a CRM, Fathom wins. Neither is better for every team, so run both on 3 real meetings before deciding.
granola-vs-fathom.29: Yes. The free plan includes unlimited recordings and transcriptions plus instant AI summaries. Some AI features carry a "limited use" tag, and Premium costs $16 a month billed yearly. Since it works with Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, the free plan is useful for most US teams from day one.
granola-vs-fathom.30: Partly. The free Basic plan includes AI notes and chat, but it keeps only 30 days of meeting history. Business costs $14 per user per month and removes the history limit. Students and accepted startups can get 12 months of Business free, and registered nonprofits get 50% off, through Granola's help center programs.
granola-vs-fathom.31: No. Granola transcribes your computer's audio and writes notes, but it does not record video. Clipping and sharing moments is a Fathom feature. If you need to replay a moment, such as a customer's exact wording, that makes Fathom the better fit; people who only need the notes are fine with Granola.
granola-vs-fathom.32: Zoom and Google Meet work with both. Fathom joins as a recorder, while Granola captures audio from your desktop app on Mac or Windows, and only Fathom also supports Microsoft Teams. Granola needs its app open during the call, whereas Fathom joins automatically from your calendar, which makes it easier to standardize across a team.
granola-vs-fathom.33: Lynkk combines bot and bot-free capture, in-person recording, and follow-up work like Jira tickets. It is free for 5 notes a month and $15 a month on Pro. It also prepares a Meeting Brief before each call and answers questions during it with Cue on Pro, which neither Granola nor Fathom offers.
